angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 554,784 km at 37.66 pc = 0.2 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 26.5541 +/- 0.0114 mas (same row, RUWE 1.02): 37.66 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.797 (0.780 to 0.815) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source): 554,784 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.791 (0.739 to 0.831) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4731 +/- 1.6 K from Andrae et al. (2023), A&A 674, A27 (Gaia DR3 GSP-Phot), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 5209903017765189760: teff_gspphot 4730.7305 K (16th-84th percentiles 4728.757-4731.951), the temperature FLAME used (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202243462). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Andrae et al. (2023), A&A 674, A27 (Gaia DR3 GSP-Phot), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 5209903017765189760: teff_gspphot 4730.7305 K (16th-84th percentiles 4728.757-4731.951), the temperature FLAME used (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202243462)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/ceibo.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.533, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 63454 (pscomppars): spectral type K4 V, from Moutou et al. 2005 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2005A&A...439..367M/abstract)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, HD 63454: main object type *, Star

luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 63454 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.592, from Moutou et al. 2005 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2005A&A...439..367M/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 63454 (pscomppars): age 1 Gyr, from Moutou et al. 2005 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2005A&A...439..367M/abstract)

spinInclinationSource: Computed here from this record's rotation period, projected rotation speed and radius (0.797 solar radii): sin i = v sin i × P / (2πR) = 0.390. Not a measurement of the axis: the three numbers come from different papers.
